item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Tehran Dismisses U.S. Cease-Fire Offer as Israel Plans New Attacks
item.summary: Tehran rejected U.S. terms to end the war and offered its own, including a demand for reparations. Israel plans to ramp up its attacks to meet its goals before a cease-fire.

item.title: Cheap Drones Remain Wild Card in Iran war
item.summary: Stopping Iran’s production of drones is critical to opening the Strait of Hormuz and halting its attacks on Gulf nations. But can it be done?

item.title: Trump Says He’s Talking With Iran. Iran Says He’s Not. Here’s Why.
item.summary: The president has domestic and international political motivations for touting negotiations to end the war. Iran has similar ones to deny discussions.

item.title: U.S. and Iran Are Talking About Ways to End the War: What to Know
item.summary: The United States is discussing ways to end hostilities with Iran, even as the Pentagon dispatches more troops.

item.title: U.S. Circulates Iran Peace Plan While Sending Troops to the Middle East
item.summary: The 2,000 paratroopers heading to the region may give President Trump more leverage in negotiations, but they also leave him with the option of doubling down on military force.

item.title: Iran’s Attacks Force U.S. Troops to Work Remotely
item.summary: Iran has severely damaged several American military bases in the Middle East, officials say.

item.title: Ukraine Finally Got Battlefield Momentum. Now Comes a Russian Offensive.
item.summary: Moscow’s forces are intensifying their attacks in southern Ukraine after Kyiv made rare gains along the front.

item.summary: The United Nations resolution was led by the president of Ghana. Israel and Argentina also voted against it.

item.summary: Syed Asim Munir’s role demonstrates Islamabad’s acute exposure to regional instability and newly found geopolitical relevance.
